claims.text: At approximately 1000 °C and above, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
At approximately 1000 °C and above, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The multielement WTaTiVZr composition produces significant lattice distortion.
The proposed lattice distortion arises from atomic-size and elastic-modulus mismatches among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
Lattice distortion lowers the effective Peierls barrier in WTaTiVZr.
A lower effective Peierls barrier enhances dislocation nucleation and mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion activates additional slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced dislocation mobility produces more efficient dynamic recovery.
Enhanced dislocation activity and dynamic recovery delay crack initiation relative to pure tungsten.
Dislocations dominate the time-dependent plastic deformation of TaTiVWZr.
Dislocation processes in TaTiVWZr are thermally activated.
WTaTiVZr is a homogeneous, equimolar BCC solid solution in the proposed initial state.
The WTaTiVZr alloy and pure-tungsten control can be prepared with comparable microstructures and identical processing histories.
Fusion plasma-facing components operate in severe high-temperature, high-heat-load environments.
Approximately 1000 °C and above is the applicable temperature regime for the proposed WTaTiVZr mechanism.
Dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr should be more restricted at lower temperatures.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will show a lower yield-stress drop.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will show enhanced dislocation activity.
Pure tungsten has a high ductile-to-brittle transition and limited plastic deformation under high-temperature service.
The constituent elements of TaTiVWZr are reduced-activity metals suitable for easier post-service recycling in nuclear applications.

contradictions.description: The comparison is described as having identical processing histories and comparable microstructures, but the tungsten control is left ambiguously as either as-sintered or recrystallized. Those are materially different initial states and do not define a single matched control.
Fracture toughness is a stated outcome and measurement, but the detailed falsification design specifies only tensile and creep tests and does not specify a fracture-toughness test.
